evals.prompt: My service `checkout-api` in workspace `payments-prod` just went CrashLoopBackOff. Tell me what's wrong and how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Reads troubleshooting.md, resolves clusterId/namespace, lists pods, pulls previous container logs + events, classifies OOM vs probe vs app error, proposes a concrete manifest edit and asks approval before apply_manifest.
expectations: Does not conclude health from DEPLOY_SUCCESS or get_application alone
Calls list_k8s_pods (or equivalent) and inspects reason / container states before proposing a fix
Uses get_k8s_pod_logs with previous:true on CrashLoopBackOff
Corroborates exit 137 with events/metrics before calling it OOM
Edits from the live activeDeployment.manifest (full replace) and validates before apply
Asks for approval before apply_manifest

evals.prompt: Deploy this HuggingFace model for me: https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in workspace llm-dev. Use whatever GPU we have.
evals.expected_output: Resolves workspaceId, calls get_model_deployment_specs, handles gated HF token via secret FQN, prefers isAvailableInWorkspace, validates and applies a service manifest, then verifies pods and offers Gateway + smoke-test next steps.
expectations: Calls get_model_deployment_specs (not hand-written vLLM YAML from memory)
Resolves workspace via list_workspaces and uses workspace.id as workspaceId
Uses a secret FQN for HF token if the model is gated — never asks the user to paste the raw token
Prefers deployments with isAvailableInWorkspace: true
validate_manifest then apply_manifest; verifies with list_k8s_pods after apply
Mentions post-deploy smoke test and optional Gateway self-hosted registration
Prints the console link ({controlPlaneUrl}/deployments/{applicationId}) and the endpoint from the deployed manifest's ports[].host / path, not a constructed host

evals.prompt: get_model_deployment_specs failed for my any-to-any Hub model. Can we still deploy it?
evals.expected_output: Retries with an explicit pipelineTagOverride inferred from the model card / architecture, or uses similar-model recovery; does not give up at the first catalogue error.
expectations: Retries get_model_deployment_specs with pipelineTagOverride (e.g. text-generation or image-text-to-text) instead of stopping
Bases the override on Hub card / architecture family, not a random guess
If still failing, uses similar-model strategy (generate for sibling, swap artifact/model id) and re-validates
Does not invent a full vLLM service from scratch unless recovery requires it

evals.prompt: My vLLM pod on a single L4 keeps crashing during model load with `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory`, even though the catalogue suggested that GPU. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Recognises a CUDA (GPU memory) OOM rather than a container OOMKilled; treats the catalogue default --gpu-memory-utilization (~0.90, in args/env) as the likely culprit on a small GPU; lowers that flag / max length / switches quant or GPU; does not invent a top-level gpu_memory_utilization field; patches from the live manifest or regenerates, and applies with approval.
expectations: Checks main-container logs/events for CUDA OOM vs download failure vs container OOMKilled
Does not raise the container memory limit as the fix for a CUDA out-of-memory error
Calls out lowering --gpu-memory-utilization in args/env (e.g. toward 0.70–0.80) on small GPUs rather than only adding more GPUs
Does not add a top-level gpu_memory_utilization key on the service manifest
Considers max model length / quantization / larger GPU as alternatives
Patches from live manifest or regenerates via get_model_deployment_specs, then validate + approval + apply

evals.prompt: My Helm app shows DEPLOY_SUCCESS but Argo is OutOfSync and pods never became Ready. Status in the UI looks stale.
evals.expected_output: Follows rollout-argocd playbook: sync_application when appropriate, checks tfy-agent health/logs, does not treat empty tool results as healthy.
expectations: Does not declare the app healthy from DEPLOY_SUCCESS alone
Uses sync_application / Argo sync guidance from failure-modes/rollout-argocd.md when OutOfSync
Checks tfy-agent / status publishing when UI state is stale
Treats empty list_k8s_* / log results as possible visibility gaps, not proof of health

evals.prompt: Scale my model service to zero when idle for 15 minutes, and pin chat sessions to the same replica for prefix cache.
evals.expected_output: Edits the live service manifest for auto-shutdown / Elasti scale-to-0 and sticky session label; explains cold-start and best-effort stickiness; validate + apply with approval.
expectations: Uses autoscaling / scale-to-0 fields from schema/docs (Elasti idle timeout), not pause/resume alone
Adds tfy_sticky_session_header_name (or schema-equivalent sticky config) and tells the client which header to send
Warns about cold start on scale-from-zero and best-effort sticky routing
Edits live manifest, validates, asks approval before apply

evals.prompt: Create a notebook in workspace ml-sandbox so I can explore this dataset, and give me the URL.
evals.expected_output: Authors a notebook application from schema, applies with approval, returns the console link and the notebook URL from list_applications; covers OAuth/login expectations from notebook-ssh playbook.
expectations: Uses get_manifest_json_schema for notebook (not service)
Sets workspace_fqn correctly and validate_manifest before apply
Mentions auth / OAuth login behavior for notebook access
Returns the console link and the notebook URL from list_applications → activeDeployment.metadata.endpoints; does not call generate_deployment_endpoint for a notebook (it rejects that type)

evals.prompt: list_application_events returned nothing for my model StatefulSet but the pod is CrashLooping. Is it healthy?
evals.expected_output: Does not treat empty application events as healthy; falls back to list_k8s_events / pod logs; notes StatefulSet event visibility caveat.
expectations: Does not conclude healthy from empty list_application_events
Falls back to list_k8s_events and get_k8s_pod_logs
Mentions that application-scoped events can miss StatefulSet-backed workloads

evals.prompt: My vLLM pod has been Pending for 10 minutes with FailedScheduling insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Follows pending-scheduling: reads FailedScheduling + pod describe + GPU nodes, then checks Karpenter/autoscaler (get_cluster_autoscaler_logs and/or NodeClaims) instead of stopping at the pod event or looking for app logs.
expectations: Does not call application container logs as the primary signal for a Pending pod
Reads FailedScheduling events and describes the pod for GPU requests/tolerations
Calls get_cluster_autoscaler_logs and/or lists Karpenter NodeClaims/NodePools when no suitable GPU node exists
On AWS, handles get_cluster_autoscaler_logs 501 by using NodeClaim status rather than giving up

evals.prompt: How is vLLM deployed on TrueFoundry? Do you run multiple models in one pod? How do GPUs and model download work?
evals.expected_output: Answers from model-serving-faq: one service per model, TP in-pod, dedicated GPUs by default, HF/artifact download to /opt/truefoundry with optional cache PVC, no shared multi-model fleet.
expectations: States each model is its own service / dedicated vLLM container, not a shared multi-model fleet
Explains multi-GPU as tensor parallelism in the same pod
Describes download into cluster (HF or truefoundry-artifact) and cache PVC vs emptyDir
Does not claim vLLM-native KV-cache autoscaling as a current platform default

evals.prompt: We only changed our model service autoscaling min/max from 1-2 to 2-3 in production and it created a new ReplicaSet and killed the existing pod. Is this a bug?
evals.expected_output: Reads the app rollout_strategy; explains a replica edit is a new revision; with max surge 0% / unavailable >0 (common model default) the old pod can go down before the new one is Ready — expected, not necessarily a bug; proposes surge/minReplicas/canary/cache mitigations.
expectations: Does not call it a definite platform bug without reading rollout_strategy
Explains new revision + rolling update behavior for replica-only changes
Calls out max_surge_percentage 0 with few replicas as a downtime cause for GPU models
Suggests concrete mitigations (raise surge if capacity, minReplicas>=2, canary, cache PVC)

evals.prompt: Our production deploy has been stuck in WAITING for over 10 minutes and no new pods are coming up. Other apps on this cluster look stuck too. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: Checks blast radius (one cluster vs all), suspects tfy-agent publish/sync, recommends restarting only Deployment tfy-agent (not proxy/SDS/ESO), gives kubectl/Argo steps if tools cannot delete agent pods; mentions NATS if all clusters affected.
expectations: Establishes whether the issue is one app, one cluster, or all clusters
Mentions NATS/control plane when symptoms span all clusters
Recommends restarting only the main tfy-agent Deployment/pods, not tfy-agent-proxy, sds-server, or external-secrets siblings
If tfy-agent Deployment is not found via tools, instructs Argo CD or kubectl restart of deployment/tfy-agent rather than guessing other workloads
Does not rewrite the application manifest as the first fix for cluster-wide WAITING
Gives the user the `kubectl rollout restart deployment/tfy-agent` command to run rather than claiming to have restarted it, and does not suggest deleting pods by label

evals.prompt: My vLLM service shows reason OOMKilled and restarts every few hours. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Treats OOMKilled as the container hitting its memory limit: pulls memory metrics and the applied memory limit, distinguishes limit-too-low from a leak, and proposes raising memory resources from the live manifest — not lowering --gpu-memory-utilization.
expectations: Confirms reason OOMKilled from list_k8s_pods rather than inferring from exit code 137
Pulls memory usage via list_app_metric_charts → get_application_chart_data and compares it with the applied memory limit
Proposes raising memory_limit / memory_request (or flags a leak if usage climbs steadily) rather than changing --gpu-memory-utilization
Edits from activeDeployment.manifest, validates, and asks approval before apply_manifest

evals.prompt: I want to understand what is happening with this service - emotion-class-svc - why is this not working?
evals.expected_output: Lists applications named emotion-class-svc; when more than one workspace has one, shows the matches with their workspaces and asks which the user means before diagnosing anything.
expectations: Calls list_applications filtered by the name
If more than one workspace has an application with that name, lists them with their workspaces and asks which one — does not diagnose the first match
Only after the application is settled, resolves clusterId/namespace and reads pod state with list_k8s_pods

evals.prompt: Bump the replicas of checkout-api in workspace payments-prod to 3.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an update: fetches the deployed manifest, changes only replicas, keeps every env var, secret, resource and probe, validates, and applies with approval — without rebuilding.
expectations: Finds checkout-api in payments-prod and calls get_application for activeDeployment.manifest
Changes only the replica count and carries every other field over — does not build a fresh manifest from the schema
Uses apply_manifest of the edited manifest (no rebuild, no tfy deploy) even if the app was originally built from source
validate_manifest, then apply_manifest with approval, then confirms pods are running

evals.prompt: Deploy the FastAPI app in this repo as a service in workspace dev-ws and expose it on port 8000.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether the name is taken in dev-ws, asks for inputs it would otherwise guess, sets a host on the exposed port from generate_deployment_endpoint, builds with build_source local via tfy deploy, reads the build logs, and prints the console link and the endpoint from the deployed manifest.
expectations: Checks list_applications for the name in dev-ws before asking questions
Takes workspace_fqn from list_workspaces
Sets ports[].host from generate_deployment_endpoint for the exposed port instead of inventing one
Uses build_source: local with local_build decided by `docker info`, and tfy deploy rather than apply_manifest or tfy apply
Reads the build logs (builds.md) instead of reporting success when the deploy call returns
Prints the console link and the endpoint from the deployed manifest

evals.prompt: Add a rate limit of 100 requests per minute for the team ml-team across all models.
evals.expected_output: Reads rate-limiting.md, fetches the existing rate-limit config and merges the new rule into it, keeps the config's top-level name, validates then applies, and links the rate-limiting settings page with the real controlPlaneUrl.
expectations: Reads ai-gateway/references/rate-limiting.md before building anything
Calls get_gateway_config and merges the new rule with the existing rules rather than replacing them
Includes the existing config's top-level name in the manifest
Calls validate_manifest and waits for valid: true before apply_manifest (not in the same parallel batch)
Shows {controlPlaneUrl}/llm-gateway/settings?configTab=rate-limiting with the real controlPlaneUrl from get_me
